title: Abstract 181: The combination of a novel retinoid compound with standard chemotherapy increases cytotoxicity in an ovarian cancer cell line
abstract: Abstract                Background: Retinoids are a class of chemotherapeutic agents that have been studied in a variety of malignancies and are known to play an important role in cellular proliferation and apoptosis. 9cUAB30 is a novel retinoid compound that has been shown to demonstrate anti-tumor activity in breast cancer and in acute promyelocytic leukemia. The objective of this study was to determine if 9cUAB30, alone and in combination with carboplatin, has cytotoxic effects on ovarian cancer cells.                Methods: The ovarian cancer cell line A2780 was cultured in 96-well plates for 24 hours. Carboplatin at doses of 15 and 30 µM was added 24 hours after plating (Day 1). 9cUAB30 at doses of 0.5, 1, and 3 µM was also added at 24, 72, and 120 hours after plating (Days 1, 3 and 5). On Day 7, cell viability was assessed using adenosine triphosphate (ATP) assays.                Results: Mean cytotoxic values (expressed as % of untreated control) were calculated for 9cUAB30 monotherapy. On average, 6% cytotoxicity was observed at the lowest dose (0.5 µM,) compared to 48% cytotoxicity at the medium dose (1 µM) and 66% cytotoxicity at the highest dose (3 µM). Addition of 9cUAB30 at doses of 1 and 3 µM significantly reduced cell viability (p&lt;0.01) compared to controls. When used in combination with carboplatin (30 µM), 9cUAB30 at doses of 0.5, 1 and 3 µM resulted in 71%, 85% and 91% cytotoxicity, respectively. When used in combination with a lower dose of carboplatin (15 µM), 9cUAB30 at doses of 0.5, 1 and 3 µM resulted in cytotoxicity of 67%, 83% and 89%, respectively. Addition of 9cUAB30 to carboplatin at either 15 or 30 µM significantly reduced cell viability when compared to carboplatin alone (p&lt;0.01).                Conclusion: In previous studies of acute promyelocytic leukemia, a dose of 5 µM 9cUAB30 was commonly used for in vitro studies. In ovarian cancer, lower doses of this novel retinoid can be used to achieve significant cytotoxicity. The combination of carboplatin and 9cUAB30 provided additional ovarian cancer cellular cytotoxicity. Further in vivo studies in ovarian cancer xenografts models are underway to determine if this novel retinoid compound enhances efficacy in combination with standard chemotherapy.
